claims.reason: The part about noting the time of the last caffeine serving is backed only indirectly: both sources give an interval counted from bedtime (NHS 6 h, meta-analysis 8.8 h for the stated coffee dose), which presupposes knowing that time. The part 'i jak śpisz' (observing one's own sleep) is not advised by either snapshot: the NHS page and the abstract contain no advice to monitor or record one's own sleep or caffeine timing. The sentence is explicitly labelled by the editors as their own proposal.

scope_gaps.note: Both sources count the interval from bedtime or going to bed ('prior to bedtime', 'before going to bed'), not from sleep onset; a reader could take 'pora snu' as the moment of falling asleep. The sources do not test 'keeping an interval' as an intervention with a sleep outcome beyond the abstract's pooled effect.
No snapshot advises self-monitoring of caffeine timing or sleep; the sources only give interval thresholds.

A reader might assume the sources show that moving the last caffeine earlier resolves sleep difficulty. The NHS page lists it as a habit change within general insomnia self-help and the abstract reports pooled sleep measures after caffeine; neither tests the shift as a treatment, and the sentence does not claim an outcome.

The NHS page gives the 6-hour figure as self-help advice with no dose, no evidence basis and no effect size; it is not equivalent to the meta-analysis threshold (8.8 h for 107 mg coffee). The sentence does not claim otherwise.

Abstract only: population, how the 8.8 h threshold was derived and heterogeneity are not visible. The threshold is tied to the stated coffee dose (107 mg per 250 mL); a reader might assume it holds for any coffee serving, the sentence does not say so.
Abstract only: the method by which the threshold was computed from the pooled data is not available.

The 45 min is the abstract's pooled mean over studies of different doses, timings and populations; the abstract gives no dose, timing, confidence interval or heterogeneity, and a reader might take it as the effect of any caffeine intake. The sentence says only 'w wyniku zbiorczym'.
Abstract only: it names two caffeine sources (coffee and pre-workout supplement); the full text could give further sources, the sentence does not say 'only'.
Grade A is editorial and not checked; only the abstract was read, so the design label rests on the title and abstract, not on the full text.

Both intervals are measured from bedtime / going to bed, not from falling asleep; the two figures answer different questions (NHS: general insomnia self-help; meta-analysis: avoiding reduced total sleep time for a stated dose).

A reader might assume the thresholds scale with other doses; the abstract ties each threshold to the stated dose and does not say how it changes with other doses. The sentence does not claim otherwise.
